signals.title: JPY/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers JPY as the weekly leader at +0.754% across 7 pairs while NOK lags at -0.990% across 2 pairs, generating a wide 1.744% leader-to-laggard spread that exceeds the 1.20% critical threshold. The BoJ Summary of Opinions confirmed board members are actively debating faster rate hike timing following the September policy meeting, reinforcing monetary normalization. Conversely, NOK faces headwinds from crude softness as WTI declines 1.00% to $89.5, despite a nominal rate deficit where BoJ at 1.25% trails Norges Bank at 4.50%. USD/NOK trades above its technical anchor at 9.604, holding above its SMA20 (9.390), SMA50 (9.427), and SMA200 (9.563) cluster to confirm broad NOK vulnerability. Trade bias: Bullish JPY against European laggards, short NOK on cross-asset divergence. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI at 09:00 UTC and US ISM Manufacturing at 14:00 UTC. Risk: Sharp crude oil rebound lifting energy-linked currencies and compressing the G10 performance spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew Divergence + BoJ Policy Stance
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.30, holding above its SMA20 of 156.07 while testing below the SMA50 at 158.26 and SMA200 at 158.47. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds hold net long JPY positions of +4,472 contracts at the 98th percentile of their 52-week range (z = +2.66), even after a WoW reduction of 15,597 contracts. The 25-delta Risk Reversal prints at -2.60 for the 1M tenor (indicative mid), signaling extreme institutional put skew and downside protection hedging despite USD/JPY holding firm near 158.30. A wide 265bp OIS carry advantage favors USD via SOFR at 3.88% against TONA at 1.23%, sustaining spot support while the 160.00 ceiling limits top-side expansion on heightened BoJ intervention sensitivity. Trade bias: Neutral to defensive USD/JPY; options skew points to downside vulnerability against positive carry. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: US ISM manufacturing surprise accelerating yields and forcing USD/JPY through 159.00 toward 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Real Yield Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1328, positioned entirely below its SMA20 (1.1501), SMA50 (1.1535), and SMA200 (1.1618) to reflect entrenched downside momentum. FX options reflect an elevated volatility risk premium of +2.3%, with 1M ATM implied volatility at 5.8% running significantly above 30-day realized volatility of 3.5%, pointing to active institutional downside hedging rather than complacency. Macro fundamentals reinforce the downward drift as the US 5Y yield gained +57bp over 20D (FRED, as of Sep 29), split as real +54bp and breakeven +3bp in a real-yield-led move. The OIS rate differential between SOFR at 3.88% and €STR at 2.44% provides a 144bp carry premium supporting the dollar, leaving immediate technical support around 1.1300 exposed. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent carry drag and elevated vol hedging cap recovery. Catalyst: Euro Area Flash CPI at 09:00 UTC followed by ECB President Lagarde speech at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Eurozone headline inflation prints significantly above the 3.0% forecast, prompting an aggressive hawkish repricing in ECB policy paths.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Retail Positioning Extreme + Carry Premium
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8362, extending gains for a seventh consecutive session and trading firmly above its SMA20 (0.8202), SMA50 (0.8136), and SMA200 (0.7953) moving-average cluster. Retail sentiment displays an extreme imbalance with Retail sentiment data showing 74% short positioning, while CFTC institutional positioning reflects Leveraged Funds net short CHF at -18,620 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z = -2.30). The pair is fundamentally anchored by a dominant 400bp CB policy rate differential, with the Fed at 4.00% hiking stance against the SNB at 0.00% on hold, while 2Y sovereign yield spreads widened 35bp in the dollar's favor over the past 20 sessions to -464bp. Options markets price an elevated vol premium of +2.1% (IV 6.8% vs HV30 4.7%), underscoring upside chase risk against retail fading flow. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF, riding institutional carry divergence against crowded retail shorting. Catalyst: Switzerland CPI at 06:30 UTC and procure.ch Manufacturing PMI at 07:30 UTC. Risk: Swiss CPI prints a substantial upside surprise above 0.3% m/m, triggering an unexpected SNB policy repricing.
